comments.author: sourcery-ai
comments.body:
**suggestion (bug_risk):** Treating any failure to read `install.dat` as a prefix mismatch may obscure the root cause.

If the second `python3` call fails (e.g., missing/corrupt `install.dat`), `new_dat_prefix` becomes empty and we print that the prefix is “still "" after reconfigure”, which hides the real problem. It would be clearer to treat this as a separate error case (e.g., check that `install.dat` exists/is readable before unpickling, or check the command’s exit status) and emit a specific message for “cannot read install.dat” vs. a true prefix mismatch.

```suggestion
	        meson setup $(SETUP_ARGS) --prefix=$(PREFIX) $(BUILDDIR) $(TOPSRC); \
	        new_dat_prefix=$$(python3 -c "import pickle; print(getattr(pickle.load(open(\"$(BUILDDIR)/meson-private/install.dat\",\"rb\")), \"prefix\", \"\"))" 2>/dev/null); \
	        new_dat_status="$$?"; \
	        if [ "$$new_dat_status" -ne 0 ]; then \
	            echo "[install] FAIL: cannot read $(BUILDDIR)/meson-private/install.dat after reconfigure; refusing to install" >&2; \
	            exit 1; \
	        fi; \
	        if [ "$$new_dat_prefix" != "$(PREFIX)" ]; then \
	            echo "[install] FAIL: install.dat prefix still \"$$new_dat_prefix\" after reconfigure; refusing to install to wrong prefix" >&2; \
	            exit 1; \
	        fi; \
```

comments.body: `Block::kcache_rollback()` now clears `m_readport_exhaustion_failed`, but there are call sites that take a KCACHE snapshot, call `try_schedule_vec_candidate(...)`, and then unconditionally call `kcache_rollback(snapshot)` on failure (e.g. the PV/PS seeker in `schedule_alu_to_group_vec`). In the `add_vec_instructions` rejection path, `try_schedule_vec_candidate` sets `mark_readport_exhaustion_failed()` after its own rollback, but the caller’s rollback will clear the flag again, preventing `schedule_alu()` from seeing it and splitting the clause. Consider either (a) removing the redundant caller rollback when `try_schedule_vec_candidate` already restored KCACHE, or (b) splitting rollback into “restore KCACHE state” vs “clear failure flags”, so the failure signal survives until the outer scheduling loop consumes it.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: `readport_exhaustion_failed()` is used as a general “vec candidate rejected for local-to-group reasons” signal (see the add_vec_instructions failure path and the log text "readport or local"), but `schedule_alu()` reports this as "readport exhaustion" and the flag name implies only readport exhaustion. This makes the stderr message (and any diagnostics keyed off the flag) potentially misleading. Consider renaming the flag/message to something generic (e.g. local vec constraint failure) or, if you want to keep the readport name, only set it when the rejection is specifically due to readport exhaustion and use a separate flag for other local constraints.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: `Block::kcache_rollback()` now clears `m_readport_exhaustion_failed`, but there are call sites that take a KCACHE snapshot, call `try_schedule_vec_candidate(...)`, and then unconditionally call `kcache_rollback(snapshot)` on failure (e.g. the PV/PS seeker in `schedule_alu_to_group_vec`). In the `add_vec_instructions` rejection path, `try_schedule_vec_candidate` sets `mark_readport_exhaustion_failed()` after its own rollback, but the caller’s rollback will clear the flag again, preventing `schedule_alu()` from seeing it and splitting the clause. Consider either (a) removing the redundant caller rollback when `try_schedule_vec_candidate` already restored KCACHE, or (b) splitting rollback into “restore KCACHE state” vs “clear failure flags”, so the failure signal survives until the outer scheduling loop consumes it.

comments.body:

comments.body: `meson setup build "${pkgname}"` will fail if the `build/` directory already exists from a previous `makepkg` run (Meson requires `--reconfigure` or `--wipe` for an existing builddir). Given `pkg-mesa-gororoba` reuses `GOROROBA_PKG_DIR` across invocations, this can make repeated packaging runs non-idempotent.

comments.author: copilot-pull-request-reviewer
comments.body: If `open(log_path, ...)` fails in the child, the failure is silently swallowed and the child proceeds to `execvp` with the parent's inherited stdout/stderr, which contradicts the caller's intent to redirect output to a log file (and, for the `extract_argv` background call site, will leak `trace-cmd` chatter onto the host program's stdout/stderr). Consider `_exit(127)` on `open` failure, or at minimum redirect to `/dev/null` as a fallback.

comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Retry the foreground wait after EINTR**

When `trace-cmd start/stop/reset` runs in a process that receives an unrelated signal while this `waitpid()` is blocked, `waitpid` can return `-1` with `errno == EINTR`; this path then returns `-1` without reaping the direct child even though the command may have completed successfully. That leaves a zombie and reports a spurious tracing failure in signal-heavy applications, unlike the background branch just above which already retries on `EINTR`.

comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve driver-location output order after lowering**

When this refresh makes `nir_tgsi_scan_shader` take its `io_lowered` path, the scan re-denses `output_semantic_name[]` by numeric `gl_varying_slot`, while the interpreter still writes `store_output` to `var->data.driver_location`. On r300 SW-TCL shaders that write point size and color, `r300_draw_fill_vs_outputs` assigns driver locations in POS, PSIZ, COL0 order (`src/gallium/drivers/r300/r300_vs_draw.c:123-126`), but `VARYING_SLOT_COL0` sorts before `VARYING_SLOT_PSIZ`; after this commit enables the direct executor by default, draw labels slot 1 as color even though the interpreter stored PSIZ there, so point-size/color attributes are emitted from the wrong rows.

Useful? React with 👍 / 👎.

comments.author: chatgpt-codex-connector
comments.body:
**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Preserve one-attribute passthrough callers**

This shared helper is still used by `vl_deint_filter` and `vl_matrix_filter`, and both paths create/bind only one vertex element from the quad buffer (`vl_deint_filter.c:248-254`, `vl_matrix_filter.c:151-156`). After this change the texcoord varying reads attribute 1, so those existing gfx filter draws feed an unbound/undefined input to the fragment shader instead of the quad position the helper previously copied, producing wrong sampling coordinates for deinterlace and matrix-filter renders unless those callers get a second vertex element or keep the old position-as-texcoord path.
